neighbours.label: Gas or air forming bubbles or foam (forms tiny bubbles, gas bubbles, trapped air); promotes bubble, foam, gas. The same substances without gas or bubbles stay quiet
fire: Baking soda releases gas that forms bubbles in the batter.
Soda foams because dissolved carbon dioxide forms tiny bubbles.
Frothy lava is full of gas bubbles.
Soap traps air in a thin film of bubbles.
Divers must avoid nitrogen forming bubbles in the blood.
Beer gets its head from small gas bubbles.
The pump forces air into the tank, making foam.
Trapped air forms tiny pockets in the plastic.
quiet: Baking soda is sold in boxes at the store.
Soda costs more because of the sugar tax.
Solid lava is full of iron minerals.
Soap removes oil from a thin film of grease.
Divers must avoid sharks in the warm water.
Beer gets its taste from hops and malt.
The pump forces water into the tank, filling it.
Melted sugar forms tiny crystals on the plastic.
